$comment: C9 · what one epoch costs a running schweepd in resident memory (I-10).
Produced by: cargo test --release -p schweep-soak --test c9_server_soak -- --nocapture
MACHINE-DEPENDENT: resident memory is an allocator and kernel figure, so no test recomputes
these rows. The deterministic half of C9's measurements is c9-bounds.json, which IS
Read the 'attribution' rows first. They are the reason this gate asserts a per-epoch
coefficient rather than a flat curve: a schweepd's resident memory is O(retained log), because
schweep_log::Log keeps every sealed batch resident and one dedup token per append. That is not
a leak and this soak cannot make it flat; docs/PROGRESS.md records it against C10.
The 'unbounded_state_workload' row is here because it was the first measurement and it was
unusable: with three groups gaining a member per epoch, 6,498 bytes of growth per epoch was
part legitimate data and part whatever might have been hiding behind it. A soak whose own
workload grows cannot report a leak.

shape.sql: SELECT t.k AS k, SUM(t.n) AS s FROM t GROUP BY t.k
shape.state: bounded — the table holds five rows forever, so every byte of growth belongs to the log
shape.load: one read per epoch, one subscribe every third epoch, one register+deregister every hundredth

attribution.workload: ingest and seal only, no registration
attribution.what_it_is: schweep_log::Log's resident sealed batches plus one dedup token per append
the registration's own per-epoch cost, which is within the noise of the log's

attribution.workload: one registration, a read every epoch

at_the_committed_shape.verdict: PASSED: 1,810 bytes per epoch against a 4,096 budget, with the log accounting for 407 of them on disk and more in memory
at_the_committed_shape.note: The per-epoch figure varies between runs on one machine (1,513 to 1,810 measured); the budget is set from the attribution rows above rather than from any single run. Note also that `Curve::growth` is a FRACTION: 0.433 is 43.3%, and it is reported rather than asserted on, because a server's resident memory grows with its retained log.

unbounded_state_workload.$comment: The first, unusable measurement. Kept because the lesson is the finding.
unbounded_state_workload.why_it_was_unusable: three groups gained a member per epoch, so operator state grew without bound and the growth could not be attributed

slow_consumer.$comment: The backpressure mutation's instrument. Both numbers were measured on the same workload: 4 sources, 200 attempts each, 600-row batches (~20 KB on the wire), nothing sealed.

with_backpressure.which_bound_fired: the count bound (64 batches), at this batch width

slow_consumer.note: The budget was 160 MiB in the first version and the mutation slipped under it: only the refusal count caught the leak, and the budget — the instrument the sprint asked for — watched it happen. 32 MiB sits between the two measured peaks, so both instruments now fail on it.

one_binary_per_measurement.$comment: Every RSS-measuring test in this crate is its own test binary, because resident memory is a property of the process. The slow-consumer gate moved to testing/soak/tests/c9_slow_consumer.rs for that reason; the C9 memo-ceiling gate learned it the hard way (see c9-memo-ceiling.json).

measured_in_ci_nightly.$comment: The nightly-soak job's first run: ten times the per-push window, on ubuntu-latest, release profile. CI run 31525525249.
measured_in_ci_nightly.verdict: PASSED: 1,651 bytes an epoch at 10,000 epochs against 1,513 to 1,810 at 3,000 — the coefficient is stable across a three-fold longer window, which is what makes it a coefficient rather than an artifact of the window

the_slope_check_compared_unequal_spans.$comment: An instrument bug, found by reading a passing run's numbers rather than a failing one.
the_slope_check_compared_unequal_spans.what_it_did: compared mean(Q2) - mean(Q1) against mean(Q4) - mean(Q2): one quarter against two
the_slope_check_compared_unequal_spans.consequence: perfectly linear growth reports a ratio of 2, so a check written as 'no more than twice' only ever fired on a FOURFOLD acceleration while appearing to fire on a doubling
the_slope_check_compared_unequal_spans.how_it_surfaced: the 10,000-epoch nightly reported '4,140,080 then 8,185,777' — a ratio of 1.98, which reads as an accelerating leak and is in fact perfectly linear growth
the_slope_check_compared_unequal_spans.fix: quarter against quarter, over equal spans. Measured after the fix at 3,000 epochs: 1,188,750 then 1,106,778 — the same twice, which is what linear growth should report
the_slope_check_compared_unequal_spans.lesson: a metric that cannot report 1 for the null hypothesis cannot report anything
